# Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers — concept pack

> Source-anchored research for Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers. Run status: COMPLETED.

## Vocabulary

Terms this pack was harvested with, grouped by their relation to the concept; counts are units matched / sources. Zero-hit terms are listed under Coverage. On every unit line, `keywords:` names the terms that matched.

- **self**: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers (16/2)

## Definitions

- [statement] Pub/Sub API is not a transport-only replacement for every legacy Streaming API subscription: it supports change data capture and high-volume platform events, but excludes PushTopic events, generic streaming events, and standard-volume platform events. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/supported-event-types.html · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers

## How it works

- [statement] Streaming API pushes available events without client control of the delivered count. Pub/Sub API lets the consumer request a count based on its processing capacity, providing subscription flow control. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-streaming/guide/pubsub-api-streaming-api-comparison.html · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html
- [statement] Pub/Sub CDC headers include changedFields and nulledFields that Streaming API omits; nulledFields, diffFields, and changedFields require further processing. Consumers must account for this header difference when migrating. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-streaming/guide/cdc-event-diff-pubsub-cometd.html · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers
- [statement] Pub/Sub documentation recommends saving replay_id from empty FetchResponse keepalives as well as processed events, because keepalives can advance the replay position and reduce seek time after reconnecting. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Both APIs can replay retained CDC events after disconnection; Pub/Sub does not uniquely provide replay. The documented retention is three days for CDC and high-volume platform events, and a consumer cannot rely on events remaining after that window. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-streaming/guide/using-streaming-api-durability.html · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html
- [statement] Pub/Sub Subscribe still needs connection recovery: an error stops the long-lived connection, and the client must retry Subscribe to create a new connection. Changing the replay position requires a new Subscribe call because only the first FetchRequest replay option is honored. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers
- [statement] Recovery options change names when migrating: Streaming API uses a specific replay ID, -1 for new events, and -2 for all retained events; Pub/Sub Subscribe uses CUSTOM with replay_id, LATEST, and EARLIEST respectively. Retrieving all retained events can slow performance in both APIs. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-streaming/guide/using-streaming-api-durability.html · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] In both APIs, the default subscription starts with new events rather than recovering the backlog. A reconnecting consumer should explicitly resume from a saved replay position when it needs missed events. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-streaming/guide/using-streaming-api-durability.html · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/references/methods/subscribe-rpc.html
- [statement] Pub/Sub change-event parsing also changes header and date handling: changedFields and nulledFields are included beyond the Streaming API header fields; nulledFields, diffFields, and changedFields require further processing; Pub/Sub dates use Epoch time rather than the Streaming API UTC representation. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-streaming/guide/cdc-event-diff-pubsub-cometd.html · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers
- [statement] For either consumer transport, persist replay positions rather than calculating the next position: replay IDs are opaque, need not be contiguous, and are used to recover retained events after disconnection. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-message-durability.html · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-streaming/guide/using-streaming-api-durability.html

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Moving a Case change-event consumer from Streaming API to Pub/Sub API requires a wire-format change: CometD/Bayeux and JSON become gRPC/protocol buffers and an Apache Avro binary payload. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-streaming/guide/pubsub-api-streaming-api-comparison.html · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-streaming/guide/cdc-event-diff-pubsub-cometd.html
- [statement] A migrated CDC parser must distinguish unchanged fields from cleared values: Streaming API omits null and unchanged record fields, whereas Pub/Sub API includes all record fields and represents unchanged and unpopulated fields as null. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-streaming/guide/cdc-event-diff-pubsub-cometd.html · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers
- [statement] Streaming API documentation now specifies that, starting with API version 68.0, successful /meta/connect responses emit updated per-channel replay IDs in ext.replay[<channel>]. Comparisons claiming CometD never advances a cursor without event payloads must therefore be qualified by API version. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-streaming/guide/using-streaming-api-durability.html · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers
- [statement] A CometD GitHub issue reports missed Salesforce events while the client remained subscribed and long polling. The maintainer said the initial evidence could reflect bugs or application mistakes and requested connection-level and DEBUG evidence; the report does not establish a confirmed Salesforce or CometD defect. (low confidence) — https://github.com/cometd/cometd/issues/1142 · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers
- [statement] Salesforce recommends Pub/Sub API for new external applications consuming platform events or change data capture events. Both Pub/Sub API and Streaming API can consume these event categories. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-streaming/guide/cdc-event-diff-pubsub-cometd.html · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-streaming/guide/pubsub-api-streaming-api-comparison.html
- [statement] Switching transport does not extend the documented CDC retention window: Pub/Sub API and Streaming API both support replay of retained change events for 72 hours; Salesforce does not guarantee storage beyond that window. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-message-durability.html · keywords: Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-streaming/guide/using-streaming-api-durability.html

## Research summary — Salesforce Streaming API CometD versus Pub/Sub case consumers

For external Case-event consumers, Streaming API and Pub/Sub differ in protocol, encoding, flow control, and CDC payload semantics. Streaming API uses CometD/Bayeux and JSON; Pub/Sub uses gRPC and Avro payloads with explicit demand. A migration must adapt decoding and field-change handling. Both APIs support replay within retention, so cursor persistence and deliberate restart choices matter with either API. Current Streaming API documentation also describes per-channel cursor updates starting with API version 68.0. Historical missed-event reports provide troubleshooting leads rather than proof of a universal protocol defect.
